newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends down against dollar on import deals.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends down against dollar on import deals.

text.p: The South Korean won ended Tuesday's trading lower against the U.S. unit due to continued dollar demand for importer settlements, dealers said.

Contrary to expectations, the central Bank of Korea did not agressively intervene in the spot market to keep the won above 880. It was instead seen offering to sell dollars at 896.50 in three-month and at 911.00 in six-month forward trading.
The central bank has refused to comment on talk of its intervention in interbank trading.
The won closed the session at 883.10 after opening at 881.50. It ended Monday's trading at 880.00.
Dealers said the central bank was trying to keep the won from falling below the 885 mark.
"Whether the market breaks the last resistance line of 885 won tomorrow dictates whether the dollar could reach 900," a local dealer said.
The base mid-rate was seen pegged at 882.60 on Wednesday, against Tuesday's 879.80.
